newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO says hidden reserves Dfl 4.02 bln.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO says hidden reserves Dfl 4.02 bln.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Thursday it had hidden reserves of 4.02 billion guilders ($2.1 billion) at December 31.
ABN AMRO, the largest Dutch bank, was revealing for the first time the size of its provision for general contingencies, designated by the Dutch acronym VAR.
Analysts had forecast the bank's VAR at between four and five billion guilders.
Dutch banks have been ordered to unveil their VAR, or hidden reserves, by the year 2000 to comply with changes to European Union rules.

The bank also said 2.00 billion guilders of the hidden reserves was transferred to a fund for general banking risks, with the remainder being transferred to a general reserve effective January 1, 1997.
The new open fund will carry the acronym FAR.
The new FAR fund is designed for unexpected loan losses, potential claims and law suits and, under normal circumstances, no deductions will be made from this fund.
Actual loan losses, which were previously covered by additions to the VAR fund, will from 1997 by deducted directly from each banks' profit and loss account.
Analysts expect a one-off rise in bank profits as a result of these changes because they will cut provisions for loan losses, having over-provided for such losses in the past.
